notes: Requested by the user 22-Aug-2026 via a pasted Python/Selenium reference script (which used the URL https://mtradeasia.com/exchange — confirmed correct on direct inspection, unlike two of the other three sites in that same script). Verified LIVE 22-Aug-2026 via direct browser automation (mcp__claude-in-chrome), not WebFetch/WebSearch — WebFetch converts a page to markdown through a summarizing model and cannot see real DOM structure or confirm JS-rendering, which is exactly why this step was needed before writing this adapter. Confirmed via fetch(location.href) from within the live page: the raw HTML response DOES already contain the '.exchange-arrow-row' row skeleton and the 'Counter Exchange Rates' heading (both server-rendered), but does NOT contain the string 'RENMINBI' or any other currency name/rate value anywhere in that raw response (grep-confirmed on the actual fetched text) — the rows are structurally present but their currency name, buy rate, and sell rate content is filled in by client-side JavaScript after load. This is the same 'skeleton present, values missing' pattern as Taj Muhabath, not the same as My Money Master (which is Pfully server-rendered). Playwright is therefore required for the primary (only) extraction path. Real CNY row observed live: '100 CNY / CHINESE RENMINBI', We Buy 59.2199, We Sell 61.8000 (22-Aug-2026, no branch selected — this page's rate table is NOT branch-specific; branch selection on this page only changes which physical branches are shown/highlighted elsewhere on the page, not the Counter Exchange Rates table, which is a single site-wide list). The page also offers a 'Digital Rates' tab (prepaid card rates) as an alternative to the default 'Counter Rates' tab this adapter reads — Counter Rates is what loads by default with no interaction required, and is the correct one per the project's CNY SELL scope (counter/cash rate, not a prepaid-card rate).
requiresBrowserAutomationReason: Confirmed live via fetch(location.href) executed from within the loaded page: the raw HTTP response contains the '.exchange-arrow-row' row markup and column headers (We Buy / We Sell) but zero occurrences of any currency name or numeric rate anywhere in that response — every row's actual content (currency, buy, sell) is populated by client-side JavaScript after the initial load. A plain HTTP fetch + HTML parse cannot see this data at all.
playwrightFallbackReason: Playwright IS the primary (and only) path here, not a fallback — there is nothing simpler to fall back FROM (same situation as Taj Muhabath).
branchNotes: The Counter Exchange Rates table on this page is a single site-wide list, not per-branch — confirmed live 22-Aug-2026 (the page separately lists 14 physical branch names elsewhere on the page for 'find a branch' purposes, but that list does not gate or filter the rate table). If a future re-check finds this has changed, branchSupport should be flipped to true and this note updated — do not assume it silently stays this way forever.

primarySelector.description: Counter Exchange Rates section: each currency is one '.exchange-arrow-row' div (42 observed on the page, including the header row itself, which shares the same class — filter for a row containing a recognizable currency-name element, do not just take index 0). A data row has three column divs: [0] '.col-6' containing the unit+code (e.g. a '100 CNY') and the display name (a sibling '/ CHINESE RENMINBI'); [1] '.col-3.text-center' containing a '' with the We-Buy numeric value; [2] '.col-3.text-end' containing a '' with the We-Sell numeric value. Confirmed live that the header row uses the identical column-class pattern (col-3 text-center for its 'We Buy' label, col-3 text-end for its 'We Sell' label) in the same left-to-right order as the data rows, so Buy-then-Sell column order is verified, not assumed.
primarySelector.matchStrategy: Enumerate all '.exchange-arrow-row' elements. For each, read the row's full text content and check it contains '/ ' followed by config.currencyDisplayNames[currencyCode] (case-insensitive) — e.g. '/ CHINESE RENMINBI' for CNY. Within the matching row, read the first '.currency' span found under a '.col-3.text-center' ancestor as buyRate, and the first '.currency' span found under a '.col-3.text-end' ancestor as sellRate.

waitStrategy.initialLoad: navigate to liveRateUrl, wait for '.exchange-arrow-row' to be attached (the row skeleton is present quickly since it's part of the raw HTML — see 'notes'), THEN wait an additional settle window (recommend 4-5s, matching the window used during live verification) before reading, since the actual currency name / buy / sell text inside each row arrives via a later JS/data call, not merely DOM-attachment of the row shell itself. A naive 'row exists' check without this settle window will read empty/placeholder cells.

validation.notes: Same scale/reasoning as the other two sources: this page quotes CNY per 100 units (label reads '100 CNY'), so BUY/SELL values are directly comparable in scale to My Money Master and Taj Muhabath's CNY figures without any /100 or *100 adjustment. Reject a reading where buyRate > sellRate, or where the value looks like it's missing this unit scaling.
